title: Casey, Crime Photographer
paragraphs: A newspaper crime drama about photographer Jack 'Flashgun' Casey, whose work at crime scenes repeatedly draws him into solving murders and other mysteries.

CBS crime/mystery drama adapted from George Harmon Coxe's newspaper photographer character Jack 'Flashgun' Casey. Casey works for the Morning Express, investigates crimes with reporter Ann Williams, and regularly returns to the Blue Note Cafe with bartender Ethelbert.

GRH documents the program through Flashgun Casey (July 7, 1943 to January 29, 1944) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Casey, Press Photographer (February 5, 1944 to July 4, 1945) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Crime Photographer (July 11, 1945 to March 13, 1947) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and Casey, Crime Photographer (March 20, 1947 to November 16, 1950) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are George Harmon Coxe (creator on 71 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Staats Cotsworth (performer on 71 recordings), John Gibson (performer on 69 recordings), Alonzo Deen Cole (writer on 64 recordings, creator on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), Herman Chittison (piano on 52 recordings, performer on 5 recordings, and pianist on 5 recordings), Jan Miner (performer on 54 recordings), and John Dietz (director on 54 recordings, producer on 6 recordings, and performer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, robbery, theft and stolen property, police investigation and criminal justice, framing, disguise and deception, crime-scene photography and photographic evidence, and newspaper reporting and journalism.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Pulp-to-radio detective adaptation, Commercial sponsor eras, Radio-to-television transition, and Urban newspaper crime culture.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (19 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (18 shared credited people), [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (16 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (16 shared credited people), and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (16 shared credited people).
